title: Grade 8 Science — Thu, May 21
description: Crop Production & Management — Day 4 of 5: Animal husbandry and modern agriculture
subject: science

questions.question: Animal husbandry is:
options: The science and practice of farming animals (cattle, poultry, fish, bees) for food and other products
The study of animal diseases only
questions.explanation: Animal husbandry: scientific management of livestock for meat, milk, eggs, wool, honey. Closely linked to crop farming (draught animals, manure).

questions.question: Which cattle breed is known for high milk production in India?
options: Both Sahiwal/Gir and exotic breeds like Jersey and Holstein-Friesian
None — Indian breeds give no milk
questions.explanation: India uses cross-breeding: indigenous breeds (Sahiwal, Gir, Red Sindhi) for disease resistance + exotic breeds (Jersey, Holstein-Friesian) for high milk yield.

questions.question: Poultry farming includes raising:
options: Chickens, ducks, turkeys, and geese for eggs and meat
questions.explanation: Poultry: domestic birds raised for eggs (layer farming) and meat (broiler farming). Major protein source globally.

questions.question: Fish farming (pisciculture/aquaculture) is important because:
options: It provides protein-rich food, supports livelihoods, and supplements wild fish catches
It is only done in coastal areas
questions.explanation: Aquaculture (fish farming in ponds/tanks/cages): supplements wild fisheries, provides affordable protein, creates rural employment. Both freshwater and marine.

questions.question: Green Revolution in India (1960s–70s) was associated with:
options: High-Yielding Varieties (HYV) of wheat and rice + modern inputs → dramatic increase in food production
questions.explanation: Green Revolution: HYV seeds (dwarf wheat by Norman Borlaug; rice by IRRI) + fertilizers + irrigation → India became self-sufficient in food grains from a food-deficit nation.

questions.question: High-Yielding Varieties (HYV) of crops are:
options: Traditional varieties passed down for generations
Scientifically developed varieties giving higher yield per hectare with proper inputs
Varieties resistant to all diseases without any inputs
questions.explanation: HYV seeds: developed through plant breeding, give higher yield per acre with fertilizers and irrigation. Examples: IR-8 rice, Sonalika and Kalyan Sona wheat (India).

questions.question: Organic farming avoids:
options: Synthetic chemical pesticides and fertilizers — uses natural alternatives only
questions.explanation: Organic farming: no synthetic chemicals. Uses organic manure, compost, green manure, biopesticides, crop rotation. Healthier soil long-term, but typically lower yield.

questions.question: What is the 'White Revolution' in India?
options: Operation Flood — dramatic increase in milk production making India the world's largest milk producer
questions.explanation: White Revolution (Operation Flood, 1970): Dr Verghese Kurien. National dairy grid, cooperative model (AMUL), made India the world's largest milk producer.

questions.question: Bee-keeping (apiculture) provides:
options: Honey, beeswax, pollination services (crucial for agriculture), and royal jelly
questions.explanation: Apiculture: honey (food, medicine), beeswax (cosmetics, polish), royal jelly (health product), propolis (antiseptic). Critically, bees pollinate ~70% of food crops.

questions.question: Vermicomposting uses:
options: Earthworms to decompose organic waste into rich compost (vermicompost)
questions.explanation: Vermicomposting: earthworms (especially Eisenia fetida) rapidly decompose kitchen/agricultural waste into vermicompost — excellent organic fertilizer rich in NPK and micronutrients.

questions.question: Crop variety improvement through cross-breeding aims to develop:
options: Higher yield, disease resistance, drought tolerance, better nutritional quality, and shorter growing period
Crops that grow only in cities
Crops with no seeds (to prevent reproduction)
questions.explanation: Plant breeding goals: higher yield, pest/disease resistance, drought/flood tolerance, better quality (nutrition, taste), suitable for mechanical harvesting.

questions.question: Biotechnology in agriculture (GM crops) involves:
options: Introducing specific genes into crop DNA to give desired traits (like pest resistance, drought tolerance)
questions.explanation: GM (Genetically Modified) crops: Bt cotton (India, pest-resistant), Bt brinjal, Golden Rice (vitamin A). Controversial but used widely in several countries.

questions.question: Food security means:
options: Having food locked in secure buildings
All people at all times having access to sufficient, safe, nutritious food
Only rich people having food access
questions.explanation: Food security (UN definition): physical availability + economic access + appropriate utilization of food. India's food security programs: PDS, Midday Meal, NFSA.

questions.question: The main challenge facing Indian agriculture today is:
options: Small farm size, soil degradation, water scarcity, climate change, and market access for small farmers
questions.explanation: India's agricultural challenges: 86% small/marginal farmers, soil health decline, groundwater depletion, climate extremes, low market prices, post-harvest losses.

questions.question: Sustainable agriculture means:
options: Farming that maximizes chemical use for maximum yield
Meeting today's food needs without compromising future generations' ability to produce food
Using only machines, no manual labour
questions.explanation: Sustainable agriculture: maintain long-term soil health, reduce chemical dependency, conserve water, support farmer livelihoods, maintain biodiversity — for future generations.
